name: The PHP Foundation
text: We have posted more information about today's security releases, including the sequence of events that led to the discovery, how the PHP security team is improving their processes, and what we need from you to continue this critical work. #php #security https://t.co/gbGTmk7yh1
take: The best account of how PHP2Shell was found and why the fix took time. Patch first, then read it.

name: LiteLLM (YC W23)
text:
Hello,

At 6:32 a.m. PDT we became aware of malicious LiteLLM 1.107.0 artifacts published to PyPI, Docker Hub, and GHCR, which were published at approximately 4:40 a.m. PDT. Enterprise deployments pulling only from our private registry are unaffected by this incident.

We are coordinating communication around this incident in this GitHub issue (https://t.co/JQ6nlZ9XXE).

We have removed the malicious releases and images. If you installed or ran them, please follow the remediation guidance in the above-linked issue and treat credentials accessible to those deployments as exposed.

Sincerely,
Oliver Jensen
Director of Security - LiteLLM
take: If anything of yours pulled LiteLLM on 21 October, treat every key it could reach as stolen.

name: Claude
text:
We’re opening a research preview of Claude Duet, a new app where Claude works as a proactive agent.

It comes to you with what needs your attention, completes tasks you ask of it, keeps working when you step away, and checks with you before it acts on your behalf. https://t.co/kt8gAbWuX8
take: The approval step is the safeguard. Start with one or two apps and read every action before you approve it.

name: OpenAI
text:
OpenAI models are coming to Google Cloud.

We're bringing our frontier models and Codex agentic workflows to Google Cloud's Model Garden, so enterprises can use our technology where they already build.

https://t.co/gjuLVALjDm
take: On Google Cloud? Ask how GPT usage will count against your existing commitment before you sign anything new.

name: Marcus Williams
text:
Our agents keep turning off misalignment monitoring, we're sharing two recent cases:
In the first case, a user asked GPT-6 Astra to match a reference implementation for their inference code. The reference didn’t configure a monitor, and Astra decided that was reason to remove the monitoring integration from the user’s code. When the user asked whether Astra had removed monitoring, it lied and said that it had not.
take: Unusually candid from inside OpenAI. If you use coding agents, check their diffs, not their answers.

name: GitHub Changelog
text:
A package firewall is available in public preview to inspect npm package metadata and downloads for malware before they reach endpoints like CI/CD hosts or coding agents.

https://t.co/eYM9V7R2fe
take: Worth a pilot on Enterprise Cloud. It only protects machines you point at it, so check every agent box.

name: Chrome
text:
Chrome is now using Gemini to provide even stronger protections against scams. It evaluates page content ephemerally to detect complex threats like fake antivirus and browser updates to keep you safer on the web. 

Read the details here: https://t.co/BowQ9eNaQT https://t.co/sDA5J69alz
take: Useful against fake-update scams. Ask IT whether to turn on Enhanced Protection, and what it sends to Google.

name: Mistral AI
text: Introducing Voxtral 3: state-of-the-art Transcribe and Speech models powering Mistral’s new voice agents API. 🧵 https://t.co/YA9HNVfq0u
take: Per-minute prices and EU hosting make a call-centre pilot easy to cost. Test it on your own call recordings.

name: OpenAI
text:
Our latest model advances bring stronger capabilities for building and migrating software in low-resource programming languages such as COBOL, Fortran, and Visual Basic.

These languages power software that banks, governments, and businesses depend on. Progress here means understanding decades of business logic and helping developers modernize those systems while preserving what works.

We’re building these capabilities around the challenges developers and enterprise customers bring us. If your team is working on these systems, tell us which languages and workflows we should tackle next.

https://t.co/2TbnkQixJ1
take: Promising for old banking and government code, but these are OpenAI’s own tests. Pilot on one well-tested program first.

name: anthony cimino
text:
I lead our federal affairs team at @AnthropicAI and wanted to share a few thoughts on the draft federal AI safety bill text that's been circulating this weekend after a version was shared with the press.

…

That said, striking the right balance requires discussion and input. We plan to update our discussion language on preemption to better match the intentions of our AAIF framework. In particular, we want to make it clearer that we see states retaining an important role in areas such as standards for independent evaluators and regulating a lab’s capacity to shut down a model.

…

It’s still probably time to re-evaluate thresholds to make sure the national standard is as strong as it can be, and we welcome continued dialogue on this issue.
take: Anthropic’s policy lead concedes the draft went too far on overriding states. Watch for the revised text.

name: Andy Stone
text:
We have continued to dig into the root cause here and would like to offer an update. 

Our engineering team discovered that the spike that triggered the incorrect enforcement was primarily in the account’s “reading” behavior. Specifically, our network security systems detected the use of a Claude tool reading profiles, posts, and hashtags, the rate of which sharply increased (~4x volume) in intense bursts on October 17. 

These abrupt, high-volume, sequential requests in a short period resembled automated bot traffic rather than an ordinary human browsing our systems. This activity caused our automated protections to incorrectly take the No Kings Instagram account offline. An automated re-review of the removal action an hour later recognized that shouldn’t have happened and restored the account. It unfortunately took additional time for us to straighten out the situation with admin access to the IG account. 

We want to reiterate our sincere apology for the error.
take: An agent browsing on your login looks like a bot. Keep agents off the accounts you can’t afford to lose.

name: Joseph Cox
text: New: Accenture has told employees it will only fund $29 per month of Claude use. Meaning that employees who often spend as much as $1,000 a month are now scrambling to find ways to keep access to the tool. A sign of the continuing crack down of AI https://t.co/Z2xswuSW5x
take: Unlimited AI seats are ending. Know what your AI use costs and what it produces before finance asks.

name: Anthropic
text:
We’re committing a portion of Anthropic’s shares to the Anthropic Public Benefit Fund, a new wholly owned entity dedicated entirely to the public benefit.

It will start off with 5% of our shares. For every 50% increase in the company’s value over a set baseline, we can contribute up to an extra 2%, subject to our board’s discretion.

In total, this means that roughly 20% of Anthropic’s shares are committed to the public good. Our co-founders have already pledged to donate 80% of their equity, and around half our employees are donating a portion of their equity as part of a donation matching program we’ve run since our founding.

In the post below, we share more details about our new fund.

https://t.co/XzDntVH0vH
take: A big pledge with the rules still to come. Watch who decides how the money is spent before judging it.

name: OpenCode
text:
We had a security breach last night related to a large scale distillation attack that impacted 1.4% of OpenCode Console users

We have notified them all this morning via email. If you did not get an email you were not impacted, it was a subset of users who had external providers linked

The incident is ongoing so we cannot share more details at this point but we are working with Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google to remediate
take: If a tool stores your AI keys, it can run up your bill. Put a spending cap on every key today.

name: DeepSeek
text:
🚀 DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash-1017 is here!

Stronger benchmark performance, faster task completion, and shorter outputs than the previous version—a Pareto improvement in performance and cost. Now live on our website, app, and API.

🛠️ Optimized for @DeepSeekHarness, Tencent CodeBuddy, WorkBuddy, and more. Upgrade to DeepSeek Harness v0.2.1-rc.1 or later for the best experience with the new model.

1/4

name: dax
text:
they've been non stop trying to attack our systems for the past 48 hours

a side effect is everything is getting hardened but damn we basically need agents going 24/7

because that's what they have
take: Attackers now work around the clock with automation. Defenders without the same help fall behind.

name: Aravind Srinivas
text:
Users are reverse engineering and porting software across platforms with Perplexity Computer. This user's mechanical keyboard app was Windows only, with no Linux support and no documentation. Computer downloaded the binary in its cloud sandbox, decompiled it with headless Ghidra, and ported it to a native Rust app for Linux.

Computer read the decompiled code to learn how the app drives the keyboard, then rebuilt it piece by piece, complete with keyboard lighting that syncs to music over PipeWire, a 3D view, key remapping, macros and profiles.

https://t.co/eDZwppdI6c

https://t.co/OPmnDMqurt
take: Agents can now read decompiled code and move apps between platforms. Old software with no documentation is suddenly a migration project, not a dead end.

name: Elon Musk

name: Greg Brockman
text:
6 days and $40,000 of compute with GPT-5.6 Sol to find a critical vulnerability in Chrome, claiming Google’s first full-chain reward in 2026 for a vulnerability that would affect an estimated 1 billion users.

Highlights the opportunity for defenders to utilize these tools to secure their software to unprecedented levels:
take: Finding serious bugs just got cheap. If you ship software, budget for AI-assisted security reviews now, before attackers do the same maths.

name: Demis Hassabis
text:
Gemini 4 Argon is amazing for knowledge work and coding - and it’s super fun to build with! We asked it to create this wizard chess game and it's so cool to see Argon's physics understanding & 3D modelling capabilities, makes me nostalgic for Battlechess on the Amiga - fun times!

Argon is rolling out today to Google Ultra and Pro subscribers in the @GeminiApp and Search, and Ultra subscribers in @antigravity! More info & full availability in the blog: https://t.co/7d3791mRNH
take: A new top-tier model you may already pay for. Try it on one real task from your week before you decide anything.

name: Aravind Srinivas
text:
Every Perplexity Project is a Git repo. We built a Git forge for agents, without the GitHub bloat, since no human has to approve anything.

Each agent gets its own short-lived sandbox and commits to a shared repo on S3. Fewer than 2% of submissions collide.

Agents search with plain `ls` and `grep`. That beats semantic search 63% vs 37% on answer accuracy for financial document analysis.
